You are a programming expert. 
You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From cde6bcd584b1b910d6ee8d6eb968ea5d20815444 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2016 15:20:02 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] ASoC: AMD: free memory on error

Static checkers complain if we don't free "adata" before returning.

Fixes: 7c31335a03b6 ('ASoC: AMD: add AMD ASoC ACP 2.x DMA driver')
Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>

diff --git a/sound/soc/amd/acp-pcm-dma.c b/sound/soc/amd/acp-pcm-dma.c
index 3191e0a7d273..d1fb035f44db 100644
--- a/sound/soc/amd/acp-pcm-dma.c
+++ b/sound/soc/amd/acp-pcm-dma.c
@@ -635,6 +635,7 @@ static int acp_dma_open(struct snd_pcm_substream *substream)
 					    SNDRV_PCM_HW_PARAM_PERIODS);
 	if (ret < 0) {
 		dev_err(prtd->platform->dev, "set integer constraint failed\n");
+		kfree(adata);
 		return ret;
 	}
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `sound/soc/amd/acp-pcm-dma.c`**
- A line was added to free the memory allocated to `adata` using `kfree(adata);` before returning an error code in the `acp_dma_open` function. This change occurs after a check for a failed operation (`ret < 0`), specifically when setting integer constraints fails.

### Relationships
The modification addresses a memory management issue identified by static checkers, ensuring that the memory allocated for `adata` is properly freed in the event of an error. This change is directly related to the previous commit that introduced the AMD ASoC ACP 2.x DMA driver, as it aims to fix a potential memory leak that could occur if the function exits prematurely without freeing allocated resources.
